newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gallimard would allow BNP to sell stake.
newsitem.headline: Gallimard would allow BNP to sell stake.

text.p: French publisher Gallimard is prepared to allow Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) to sell its 12.5 percent of Gallimard, financial daily Les Echos said on Wednesday.
Citing chairman Antoine Gallimard, the paper also said the publisher would create a share options plan for employees which would absorb at least five percent of Gallimard's capital.
Seven years ago Gallimard opened its capital to outside partners, with BNP and Havas each taking 12.5 percent and U.S.Scholastic taking three percent.
The publisher is also considering opening the capital of certain peripheral subsidiaries, Les Echos quoted Gallimard as saying.
He also said Gallimard no longer carried borrowings.
"Today the group is totally without debt, against a level of borrowings of over 100 million francs a few years ago," he said.
"Despite the slowdown of bookstore sales, our 1996 results will show a rise, thanks to good activity in distribution," Les Echos quoted Gallimard as saying.
In 1995 Gallimard had net profit of 51 million francs on turnover of 1.2 billion francs.
